Hattush
hat'ush
n. (a descendant of David who returned with Ezra; also a priest of the first return and a repairer of the wall)
From Hebrew Chattush, of uncertain derivation. The Chronicler places one bearer in the royal genealogy, among the sons of Shemaiah in the line of Shechaniah and Zerubbabel.

Biblical Definition

Hattush is a small name with a large placement. The Chronicler lists him in the royal genealogy after the exile: “the sons of Shemaiah; Hattush, and Igeal, and Bariah, and Neariah, and Shaphat, six” (1Ch 3:22) — the house of David, still being counted generations after the throne was gone. Ezra names him at the head of his own company: “Of the sons of Phinehas; Gershom: of the sons of Ithamar; Daniel: of the sons of David; Hattush” (Ezr 8:2). That is the order of the muster — two priestly houses, then the royal house, represented by one man travelling as a private citizen in a caravan of returning exiles. A Hattush repairs a section of the wall next to Jedaiah (Neh 3:10); a Hattush is among the priests who came up with Zerubbabel (Neh 12:2); and a Hattush seals the covenant (Neh 10:4). The son of David who goes up to Jerusalem in Ezra 8 has no crown, no court, and no prospect of one. He simply comes home when the way opens, and takes his place in a list. The line was being kept, in obscurity and by ordinary men, until the day the angel would say of one of them, “the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David” (Luk 1:32).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Hattush; in sacred history he is a descendant of David who returned with Ezra, and the name of a priest and of a repairer of the wall.

expand to see more

HATTUSH, n. A son of Shemaiah, in the line of David after the captivity.

He went up with Ezra from Babylon, being reckoned of the sons of David.

A priest of the name came up with Zerubbabel in the first return.

A Hattush, the son of Hashabniah, repaired a portion of the wall of Jerusalem.

One of the name sealed the covenant in the days of Nehemiah.

Key Scripture

1Ch 3:22 — "And the sons of Shechaniah; Shemaiah: and the sons of Shemaiah; Hattush, and Igeal, and Bariah, and Neariah, and Shaphat, six."

Ezr 8:2 — "Of the sons of Phinehas; Gershom: of the sons of Ithamar; Daniel: of the sons of David; Hattush."

Neh 3:10 — "And next unto them repaired Jedaiah the son of Harumaph, even over against his house. And next unto him repaired Hattush the son of Hashabniah."

Neh 12:2 — "Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,"

Modern Corruption

The obscurity of David's line after the exile is read as evidence that the messianic promise failed; Scripture treats the same obscurity as the promise being kept in a manner nobody would have chosen.

expand to see more

For four centuries after Zerubbabel the house of David holds no throne, and the sceptical reading concludes that the promise of an everlasting kingdom quietly lapsed. What the registers show instead is a line kept with care by men of no consequence — a Hattush in a caravan, names copied into Chronicles for a community that had no political use for them. The promise was never that David's sons would reign continuously; it was that his throne would be established for ever, and Isaiah had already described the manner: a stump, a root out of dry ground, no form nor comeliness. “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots” (Isa 11:1) — a stem is what is left when the tree has been cut down.

The second thing to draw out is how ordinary the faithfulness looks from inside. Hattush went up to Jerusalem because Ezra was going and the road was open. He is one name in one list, and he could not have known that the register he was entered in would be scrutinized by every generation of the church. That is the usual condition of obedience: a man does the next right thing without seeing what it is for. “Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord” (1Co 15:58).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Chattush (H2407), Hattush; ben David, son of David; chazaq (H2388), to repair, strengthen; netser (H5342), branch, shoot; geza' (H1503), stem, stump.

expand to see more

Hebrew Chattush (H2407) — Hattush; a descendant of David who returned with Ezra.

Hebrew Shekanyah (H7935) — Shechaniah; his ancestor in the royal genealogy of 1Ch 3.

Hebrew chazaq (H2388) — to strengthen, repair; his work on the wall in Neh 3:10.

Hebrew geza' (H1503) — stem, stump; the felled tree of David's house in Isa 11:1.

Hebrew netser (H5342) — branch, sprout; what grows out of that stump.

Usage

"“Of the sons of David; Hattush” — the royal house, travelling as passengers."

"“Hattush, and Igeal, and Bariah… six” — a line still counted when the crown is gone."

"“Next unto him repaired Hattush” — a king's descendant with mortar on his hands."
